overview: Cyprus is an island country in the eastern Mediterranean, south of Turkey. Its capital is Nicosia. Cyprus became independent from the United Kingdom in 1960. Since 1974 the island has been divided: the Republic of Cyprus controls the south, while the north is run by a Turkish Cypriot administration that only Turkey recognises. Cyprus joined the European Union in 2004.

geography.text: Cyprus is the third-largest island in the Mediterranean, after Sicily and Sardinia. The Troodos Mountains cover much of the centre and west, and the narrow Kyrenia range runs along the north coast. Between them lies the Mesaoria plain, where Nicosia stands. The island has hot, dry summers and mild winters.

history.text: Cyprus has been ruled by many powers, including Greeks, Romans, Byzantines, Venetians and Ottomans, before Britain took control in 1878. It became independent in 1960. In 1974 a coup backed by Greece's military government was followed by a Turkish invasion, and the island has been divided ever since.

events.title: Ottoman conquest
events.text: The Ottomans take Cyprus from Venice.

events.title: British control
events.text: Britain takes over the running of the island.

events.title: Coup and invasion
events.text: A coup backed by Greece's military rulers is followed by a Turkish invasion, dividing the island.

events.title: Joins the EU
events.text: Cyprus becomes a member of the European Union.

government.text: Cyprus is a presidential republic: the President is both head of state and head of government and is elected every five years. Since 1974 the island has been divided. The Republic of Cyprus, a member of the European Union since 2004, governs the south, while the north is run by a Turkish Cypriot administration recognised only by Türkiye. UN peacekeepers patrol the buffer zone between them.

economy.text: Tourism, shipping and financial services are the main parts of the economy. Cyprus has one of the largest merchant shipping fleets in the European Union. The country went through a banking crisis in 2013 and has since recovered. It uses the euro.

culture.text: Cyprus mixes Greek and Turkish culture with traces of the many empires that ruled it. Greek myth says the goddess Aphrodite was born from the sea off its coast. Halloumi, a squeaky grilled cheese, comes from Cyprus.

items.title: Aphrodite's Rock
items.text: The sea stack where, in Greek myth, Aphrodite came ashore.

items.title: Painted churches of Troodos
items.text: Mountain churches covered in Byzantine wall paintings.

items.title: Halloumi
items.text: A cheese made in Cyprus for centuries, good for grilling.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport in Cyprus, and APOEL Nicosia reached the quarter-finals of the Champions League in 2012. The sailor Pavlos Kontides won the country's first Olympic medal.

didYouKnow: Cyprus has two British military bases that are still British territory.
Nicosia is the last divided capital city in Europe.
